item.text:
**6B.10 Research Note: Abiy Ahmed (2024)**

**Bottom line:** Mixed, leaning no. There is real 2024 evidence that Abiy’s government and partners improved life chances for some groups through safety nets, refugee ID access, school WASH, health financing, and reconstruction. But the national baseline was already severe, and 2024 still featured high inflation, conflict, aid diversion, mass detention, and civilian killings. On balance, I do not see strong evidence that ordinary Ethiopians broadly ended 2024 with clearly better life chances than they inherited.

**Evidence**
- [The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia: Request of an Arrangement Under the Extended Credit Facility](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/07/29/the-federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia-request-of-an-arrangement-under-the-extended-552778) - International Monetary Fund, 2024-07-29. Claim: the program included expanding PSNP cash transfers, temporary fuel and fertilizer subsidies, and post-conflict reconstruction support to cushion the exchange-rate shock and protect vulnerable households. This is the clearest positive evidence that the government tried to soften a major shock for ordinary people. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.6, 6B.7, 6B.4, 6B.5.
- [World Bank backs Ethiopia’s reforms to promote sustainable and inclusive growth](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/07/30/world-bank-backs-ethiopia-s-reforms-to-promote-sustainable-and-inclusive-afe-growth) - World Bank, 2024-07-30. Claim: the reform package explicitly aimed to expand social safety nets, improve public spending effectiveness, and protect poor and vulnerable households. This is positive, but it is a policy intent statement rather than proof of broad lived gains by year-end. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.4, 6B.5, 6B.7.
- [Building a strong foundation to improve learning outcomes in AFE Ethiopia](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/09/05/building-a-strong-foundation-to-improve-learning-outcomes-in-afe-ethiopia) - World Bank, 2024-09-05. Claim: GEQIP-E trained 102,117 teachers, improved girls’ enrollment in historically disadvantaged regions, and supported refugee schools and students with special needs. This is strong evidence of better life chances for children in targeted groups. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.8, 6B.4.
- [Ethiopia launches inclusive ID system for refugees, boosts access to national services](https://www.unhcr.org/africa/news/press-releases/ethiopia-launches-inclusive-id-system-refugees-boosts-access-national-services) - UNHCR Africa, 2024-03-07. Claim: the refugee digital-ID rollout was designed to include refugees and asylum seekers so they could access basic national services. This is one of the clearest equal-opportunity interventions in 2024. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.8, 6B.7.
- [World Bank scales up efforts to boost the resilience of 3 million Ethiopians living in drought prone lowlands](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/03/29/world-bank-scales-up-efforts-to-boost-the-resilience-of-3-million-afe-ethiopians-living-in-drought-prone-lowlands) - World Bank, 2024-03-29. Claim: 3 million people in drought-prone lowlands were slated for resilience support, explicitly because drought, floods, conflict, and environmental degradation were already undermining livelihoods. This is meaningful, but it also underscores how harsh the starting point was. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.6, 6B.3.
- [Breaking Barriers: Empowering Girls with Clean Water and Sanitation Facilities in Ethiopia's Schools](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/01/19/breaking-barriers-empowering-girls-with-clean-water-and-sanitation-facilities-in-ethiopias-schools) - World Bank, 2024-01-19. Claim: WASH and menstrual-hygiene facilities improved attendance and reduced dropout, especially for girls. This is direct evidence of better life chances for a vulnerable group, not just aggregate service numbers. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.8, 6B.6.
- [Second Phase PROSPECTS launched in Ethiopia: empowering refugees, IDPs and host communities](https://www.unicef.org/ethiopia/press-releases/second-phase-prospects-launched-ethiopia-empowering-refugees-idps-and-host) - UNICEF Ethiopia, 2024-03-21. Claim: the program targeted education, livelihoods, protection, and infrastructure for refugees, IDPs, and host communities. This is constructive evidence for displaced people, though programmatic and limited in scale. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.6, 6B.8.
- [Bringing Back More Schools, Health Facilities to Life in Tigray](https://ethiopia.un.org/en/261479-bringing-back-more-schools-health-facilities-life-tigray) - United Nations in Ethiopia, 2024-02-23. Claim: 14 health centers, 11 schools, and 33 WASH facilities were reconstructed for 365,000 people in conflict-affected woredas. That is concrete repair of life chances in a war-damaged area. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.6, 6B.3.

**Negative / limiting evidence**
- [Ethiopia Poverty and Equity Brief: October 2024](https://documents.worldbank.org/pt/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099729001032529868) - World Bank, 2024-10-01. Claim: the Bank said living standards deteriorated across the country because of COVID-19, the Tigray conflict, Ukraine-related spillovers, droughts, and inflation, and that poverty was expected to have increased significantly since 2016. This is the strongest baseline-adjusted negative evidence against a clean “better life chances” conclusion. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.6.
- [Ethiopia | World Bank Group](https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/country/ethiopia) - World Bank, 2024. Claim: the country page says living standards deteriorated further amid double-digit inflation, debt default, conflict, and widespread food-aid dependence, while around 15 million people remained reliant on food aid. This is strong context that limits how much 2024 reforms could have improved ordinary lives. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.6, 6B.5.
- [Ethiopia | Data](https://data.worldbank.org/country/Ethiopia) - World Bank, 2024. Claim: GDP growth was 7.6% in 2024, but inflation was still 21.0% and unemployment 3.4%, so macro growth did not translate into obviously comfortable living conditions. This is mixed evidence at best: growth existed, but so did severe price pressure. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.5.
- [World Report 2024: Ethiopia](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia) - Human Rights Watch, 2024-01-12. Claim: HRW reported a coordinated food-aid diversion scheme that helped force a suspension of aid affecting about 20 million people, plus forced evictions near Addis Ababa. That is strong evidence that basic life chances were still being harmed rather than improved. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.6.
- [Ethiopia: the military executes dozens in Amhara region](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/04/ethiopia-military-executes-dozens-amhara-region) - Human Rights Watch, 2024-04-04. Claim: federal forces summarily killed dozens of civilians in Merawi. That is direct evidence that civilians in crisis zones were not experiencing safer or better life chances. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.6, 6B.8.
- [Ethiopia army attacks health care in Amhara conflict](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/03/ethiopia-army-attacks-health-care-amhara-conflict) - Human Rights Watch, 2024-07-03. Claim: soldiers seized ambulances, raided hospitals, and assaulted medical staff, disrupting access to care. This undercuts any claim of improved life chances for people in conflict-affected areas. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.6.
- [Ethiopia fighting abuses putting Sudanese refugees at risk](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/17/ethiopia-fighting-abuses-putting-sudanese-refugees-risk) - Human Rights Watch, 2024-10-17. Claim: Sudanese refugees in camps faced killings, beatings, looting, forced labor, and pressure to relocate unsafely. This is strong negative evidence for vulnerable displaced people. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.6, 6B.8.
- [End the month-long arbitrary detention of thousands in Amhara Region](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/ethiopia-end-the-month-long-arbitrary-detention-of-thousands-in-amhara-region/) - Amnesty International, 2024-11-06. Claim: a joint task force filled makeshift detention camps with thousands of civilians, and Amnesty described mass detention as a routine political tool. This is strong evidence that ordinary people’s life chances were being damaged by coercive rule. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.6.
- [Ethiopia extends state of emergency in Amhara](https://kelo.com/2024/02/02/ethiopia-extends-state-of-emergency-in-amhara/) - Reuters republished by KELO, 2024-02-02. Claim: parliament extended emergency rule amid insurgency, deaths, and abuse allegations. That is negative context for life chances because it signals continuing instability and a poor environment for ordinary households. IDs: 6B.10, also 6B.6, 6B.7.

**Search gap**
- I found more evidence of targeted improvements than of broad, durable gains in household welfare.
- The hardest missing piece is direct household-level 2024 evidence showing that most ordinary Ethiopians, especially outside donor-supported programs, were better off than they were at the start of Abiy’s rule.
- The best available record instead shows a split picture: some inclusion-oriented programs improved life chances for specific groups, but the national environment remained too unstable and inflationary to clearly say ordinary people as a whole were better off by the end of 2024.
